comparator.name: Biology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum accounts for exactly 180 EC. Years 1 and 2 each contain 60 EC of named compulsory work spanning cells, genetics, microbes, plants, animals, ecology, evolution, quantitative biology, molecular life sciences and research projects. Year 3 preserves 30 EC of genuine elective/minor/exchange space, followed by Research Project Design and Planning (6 EC), Big Data (6 EC) and an 18-EC Bachelor Project. The programme describes optional third-year specialisation through elective choice rather than formal named tracks, so no route is selected and the 30-EC choice space is not filled to improve UCR fit.

alternatives.labelRationale: The official programme explicitly develops cell biology, molecular biology, genetics, microbiology, immunity, biotechnology, bioinformatics and biomedical elective possibilities.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad biological-sciences route, this programme replaces introductory biodiversity, conservation biology, ecosystems, evolution, soils, marine biology and sustainability governance with a brain-and-behaviour gateway, neural networks, perception, higher-order functions, machine learning, psycholinguistics and image processing. Seven courses differ in each direction, producing a substantially more molecular, biomedical and computational programme.

alternatives.concept: Centres evolution, biodiversity, ecological processes and conservation while retaining cellular, physiological, microbial, laboratory and statistical foundations. alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match covers UvA Biology's full molecules-to-ecosystems identity. Two direct programme-interest clusters support coherent, substantially distinct alternatives: molecular/cellular biology linked to health and computation, and ecology/evolution/conservation linked to environmental change. All three retain feasible 24-course schedules and differ well beyond the four-course minimum. Production stops at the maximum of three defensible alternatives.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both establish broad cellular and molecular foundations; UCR also integrates health and biomedical applications.
Both introduce evolution and biodiversity across major groups of life.
Both address animal structure and function; UCR concentrates on human physiology.
Both include microorganisms; UCR focuses on host–microbe interaction and immunity rather than plant biology.
Both combine ecological principles with modelling or experimental reasoning.
Both examine genes and genomes; UCR applies molecular genetics primarily to pathology.
The official first-year restricted choice remains open.
UvA teaches dedicated scientific writing and presentation; UCR develops these skills across the curriculum.
UvA's integrated statistics and R course is distributed across UCR mathematics, statistics and data-science courses.
UvA continues dedicated academic-skills instruction; UCR embeds academic communication across courses.
UvA has a compulsory plant-biology course; UCR provides ecological and organismal context but no direct plant-biology equivalent.
UvA's biology-policy project has no single UCR equivalent; UCR programmes combine environmental science and governance courses.
UvA combines biodiversity, ecology, field identification and practical work in one compulsory course.
The programme's seven advanced Biology electives remain genuine choice space; the UCR routes instantiate different coherent biological emphases without claiming a formal UU track.
UvA requires neurobiology and behaviour; UCR offers relevant neuroscience courses in the broad and biomedical routes.
UvA's biological systems modelling is distributed across UCR mathematics, ecology and data-science courses.
UvA combines plant and animal defence; UCR covers human immunology and host–pathogen interaction more directly.
UvA integrates molecular-life-science challenges and DNA/biochemical laboratory techniques.
UvA requires a dedicated advanced evolution course; UCR covers evolutionary mechanisms in ecology and life-science courses.
Both curricula connect ecology to pollution, climate change and biodiversity loss.
Both develop quantitative biological reasoning and statistics; UCR supplies a general mathematical-statistics sequence.
UCR develops scientific communication across courses rather than in one directly corresponding course.
The compulsory 15-EC Biology research project has no scheduled UCR course counterpart; UCR's optional independent research element is shown separately.
The genuine 45-EC profiling space is preserved without invented content.
UvA requires project design and planning immediately before the Bachelor Project.
